notes: Page shows only advice on sorting pieces by colour; no building step, so nothing is added.
The left panel builds a miner minifigure (helmet with lamp, head, torso, legs). Minifigure parts are not in the parts list, so they are not recorded.
Steps 1-3 build the warning sign: black clip piece onto the triangular sign, then onto a round base, then the finished sign.

The round base looks dark and is not clearly identifiable. I assumed it is the Dark Bluish Gray Dish 2 x 2 Inverted (lego-4740), because the parts list has no other matching round piece. The black clip piece is assumed to be lego-48729b. The bar/dish port names are a best guess.
Left side builds a plunger detonator: dish base, red round brick, T-piece on top.
Right side builds the dynamite with a gauge: black clip plate, gauge tile on its stud, red dynamite sticks in the clip.
The dark round base is assumed to be lego-4740, the same as on page 3; the parts list shows one 4740 remaining, which fits.
b6 and b9 are attached by non-stud joins, so rests_on is [].
Step 1: six light bluish gray round plates and two gold crystals are dropped into the bottom half of the rock. I assumed the plates sit on its studs and the crystals lie loose inside.
Step 2: the rock top is closed over the bottom half. I listed the bottom and the six plates as what it rests on.

Right side: a finished scene. The inset shows the detonator, pickaxe and dynamite from page 4 going into the crate, with the warning sign beside it. I added the crate (b20) and pickaxe (b21) as pieces and recorded the loose placements as joins.
The miner minifigure is not in the parts list, so it is not recorded.
Step 1 places the Vehicle Base 4 x 12 as the first piece of the yellow 4x4 mining truck. The small picture at top left shows the finished truck.
Step 2: a light bluish gray 2 x 3 plate is added at each end of the vehicle base (b22).
Step 3: a black 2 x 2 plate with wheel holders is added at each end, one on each plate.

The drawing makes it hard to tell which way up the plates and wheel holders sit relative to the base. I recorded a simple stack: base, then plate, then wheel holder. The true vertical order may differ.
The rotate icon means the chassis is flipped over, so the plates and wheel holders from page 7 are now underneath.
Step 4: a red 1 x 2 brick is pressed onto two studs of the vehicle base (b22).
A yellow patch shows in the base's central recess. It is not a listed piece placed on this page; I assumed it is a sticker from the sticker sheet and did not record it.
Step 5: the red 2 x 2 seat goes on the vehicle base and the blue steering stand goes on the red 1 x 2 brick (b27).
Which studs each piece covers is read from a small drawing, so the rests_on lists are a best guess.
The 2x sub-assembly is a yellow inverted sloped 6 x 1 brick with a black 1 x 4 plate pressed into its underside recess; it is built twice.
Step 6: the two copies are placed on the vehicle base, one on each side of the seat and steering stand.
The black plate shows as a black stripe on the side of each finished piece. I recorded it as clutching the base and as joined to the slope. The exact stud contacts are a best guess.
Step 7: two light bluish gray 1 x 2 x 2 bricks go on the base, one at the front-left and one at the rear-right, next to the yellow slopes.
Step 8: four dark bluish gray wheel arches go over the wheel positions on the base end tabs. The drawing shows one in motion and three already seated, so I recorded all four on this page.
Exact stud contacts are a best guess from the small drawing.
A new sub-assembly for the front of the truck: a dark bluish gray arch brick, with two trans-orange 1 x 1 plates as lights at its ends and a yellow 1 x 4 plate along the front.
The sub-assembly is drawn turned on its side, so the stud contacts are a best guess.
Step 4: a black cheese slope is added to the bumper (b40). The arrow points at its underside, so I recorded it on b40.
Step 5: two trans-red 1 x 1 tiles (tail lights) go on the ends of the yellow 1 x 4 plate (b43), with a yellow 1 x 2 tile between them.
Step 6: a number-plate sticker goes on the yellow tile. The sticker is not recorded as a piece.
Step 9 adds no new pieces. The finished bumper sub-assembly from pages 12-13 is attached to the end of the chassis, where the tail lights face outward.
The attachment is recorded as a join because the bumper's own rests_on was fixed on an earlier page. I assumed it clutches the end studs of the base (b22).
Step 10: the red side-handle plate is added at the front end of the chassis, opposite the bumper.

Step 11: a yellow 1 x 4 brick goes on the yellow sloped sill on the near side. I read it as a brick rather than a plate because it looks tall. Which of the two sills it sits on, and which studs it covers, is a best guess.
A new sub-assembly for the front of the truck: a dark bluish gray arch brick (second lego-14520).
Step 2: a black grille tile goes between two trans-clear cheese slopes, which are the headlights.
Step 3: two dark bluish gray cheese slopes are added at the bottom corners.
The sub-assembly is drawn on its side, so the stud contacts are a best guess.
Step 12: the grille and headlight sub-assembly from page 16 is attached to the front of the chassis. A yellow 2 x 4 plate is added next to the seat area.
Step 13: the yellow curved 2 x 4 brick is added as the hood.

The unplaced list shows page 16 used one black, two trans-clear and one dark bluish gray cheese slope. On page 16 I recorded the two lower slopes (b54, b55) as dark bluish gray, so b54 is probably really black. It cannot be changed here.
The yellow pieces are read from small drawings, so which pieces they rest on is a best guess.
Step 14: two dark bluish gray cheese slopes are placed on studs of the cab, one on each side of the steering stand, toward the windscreen position.
Their exact stud positions are a best guess from the small drawing. The unplaced list still shows 3 dark slopes, so I read these two as dark bluish gray.
Step 16: a yellow 1 x 6 plate is added on the rear bed of the truck.
Step 15 is a different view of the truck and I could not identify any new piece in it.

Step 16 draws the rear bed already covered in yellow studs, which does not match step 15. Some yellow plates may have been placed in these two steps without being shown, and I could not identify them. They stay unrecorded here, so the unplaced list will show them as still unused.
Step 17 shows the truck with the 1 x 6 plate from page 19 seated on the bed. I could not find a new piece in it.
The only visible change is a sticker on the cab side, and stickers are not recorded as pieces.
Step 18: a black 1 x 4 x 2 bar with studs is added at the back of the cab, against the bed.
Step 19: a light bluish gray 2 x 2 tile sits in the bed, and a light bluish gray jumper plate is lowered onto two yellow studs beside it.
These pieces are read from very small drawings. The identification of the grey bed piece and the jumper plate, and the studs they rest on, are best guesses.
The pink piece beside the bar in step 18 could be a trans-red plate (lego-3023), but I could not confirm it, so I did not record it.

Step 20: the trans-brown windscreen goes on the dashboard slopes, and a yellow 1 x 4 panel is added along the right side of the bed. A yellow headlight brick sits behind the seat, next to the black bar. The black arch on the cab rear is the 1 x 4 x 2 bar from page 21.
Step 21: two orange round lights appear on top of the black bar and a tall yellow brick stack beside it, but I could not identify those pieces, so I did not record them.
The unplaced list shows page 5 used two trans-orange and four light bluish gray round plates. On page 5 I recorded all six as light bluish gray; two of them (b11-b16) should be trans-orange.
All identifications and stud contacts on this page are best guesses from small drawings.
Step 22, inset 1-2: a trans-red 1 x 2 plate is pressed onto the underside of the yellow curved roof brick as a rear light. A sticker then goes on the roof top; it is not recorded as a piece.
Step 22: the roof is placed over the cab. I recorded it as resting on the windscreen (b64); the exact contacts are a best guess.

The 4x box builds four wheels, each a white wheel pressed into a black tyre. Each wheel is then pushed onto a pin of one of the two wheel holders (b25, b26). Which wheel goes on which holder is a guess.
The two orange round lights on top of the black bar match no remaining unplaced piece, so I did not record them.

Step 23 shows the finished truck with the roof (b67) lifted off, to show that it comes off. The crate with the miner's tools from page 5 sits in the bed, with the rock and a minifigure beside the truck. No new pieces are added.
Advertising page for the LEGO City mining sets 4200-4204. No building step, so nothing is added.
LEGO Club advertisement page. No building step, so nothing is added.
Survey advertisement page. No building step, so nothing is added.

The unplaced list still shows many yellow pieces (doors, panel, plates, bricks), the jackhammer, one trans-red plate and some small plates. These are probably used in the pages I could not identify clearly, or in page 27, which was not provided. The model recorded here is the 4x4 mining truck.

The listed groups are loose accessories of one scene, not separate models. The booklet shows the warning sign, the detonator and dynamite in the crate, and the gold rock standing beside or in the truck (pages 5 and 24). I joined them to the truck with contact edges.

The 15 missing lines are pieces from pages I could not read clearly or from page 27, which was not provided. I added them using the parts list and the finished-truck pictures: doors, clip bricks and jackhammer, bed plates and panel, yellow brick stack, second trans-red plate, jumper, dark slope, round plates on the roll bar, and the sticker sheet.
The positions of these added pieces (which pieces they rest on) are best guesses.
The crate (b20), pickaxe (b21), detonator and dynamite from earlier pages stay as recorded. The other_joins from earlier pages stay as they are.

The booklet builds one model, the 4x4 mining truck, plus a few loose accessories: the gold rock, the warning sign, and the crate with detonator, dynamite and pickaxe. On pages 5 and 24 these are shown in or beside the truck.
I added loose joins so each accessory is connected to the truck graph. They are not fixed connections; the accessories lift out freely.
Everything recorded earlier stays unchanged.
